excluded_columns.anon_id: Patient identifier — memorisable; used only to group the split.
excluded_columns.order_proc_id_coded: Order identifier — used only to link a prediction to its culture.
excluded_columns.age: Raw age band string — replaced by age_band_ordinal and age_midpoint_years.

subsample.note: Search stages run on a PATIENT-level subsample so that within-patient correlation is preserved; the final models in Phase 7 are refitted on the full training partition.

method_1_missingness.rationale: Gradient-boosted trees treat NaN as a routed branch, so a moderately missing feature is still usable and its missingness is itself informative (an unordered procalcitonin means the clinician did not suspect severe sepsis). The threshold is therefore set high (95%) and removes only features so sparse that any split on them is fitted to a handful of patients.

method_2_low_variance.rationale: A feature whose single most common value covers >99.9% of rows cannot separate a 19.5% positive class in any useful way; it only adds a split point for the tree to overfit. Note that the audit already removed the two genuinely constant source columns (`Period_Day` = 14, `was_positive` = 1 after filtering) upstream, so this filter is a safety net rather than the main event.

method_3_correlation.rationale: The lab block is highly redundant by construction — Q25/median/Q75 of the same analyte over the same 14-day window are near-identical, and so are the class-level prior-exposure counts at 90d and 365d. Spearman is used rather than Pearson because most of these features are skewed counts. Removing one of each redundant pair shortens training and makes the SHAP attributions readable, since perfectly collinear features split their credit arbitrarily.

method_4_statistical.rationale: ANOVA F tests a linear mean shift and mutual information captures any monotone or non-monotone dependence, so they are complementary and disagree in informative ways. Chi-square was NOT used: it requires non-negative discrete counts, and the ordinal-coded categoricals and z-scored labs here violate that assumption, so it would return a number without meaning.

method_5_model_importance.rationale: Random Forest impurity importance is biased towards high-cardinality features, and `organism_clean` has 245 levels, so it is reported but not trusted alone. XGBoost average gain is the counterweight, and SHAP (Method 6) is the arbiter because it is the only one of the three that is additive and locally faithful.

method_6_shap.rationale: SHAP is the selection arbiter because its attributions are additive and locally faithful, so a feature that only matters for a small but clinically important subgroup is not averaged away as it is by gain. It is also the same machinery the application uses to explain an individual prediction, so what selects a feature and what explains it to a clinician are consistent.

method_7_rfe.rationale: RFECV was deliberately NOT used. With ~180 candidates and 1.1M training rows, cross-validated elimination would refit XGBoost several hundred times for a result that Methods 5-6 already give at a fraction of the cost. Plain RFE at a fixed target size on a 120,000-row patient-level subsample is used instead as an independent third opinion, and the feature-count sweep in the experiment section supplies the 'how many features' answer that RFECV would have provided.

selection_rule.rule: The final feature set is the candidate set with the highest PR-AUC on the held-out validation patients, with `antibiotic` and `antibiotic_class` force-retained because a single unified model cannot identify which agent it is scoring without them. The organism-blind arm is excluded from the contest because it is a measurement, not a candidate.

selection_inside_cv.interpretation: `optimism_from_global_selection` is how much PR-AUC the globally chosen feature list gains over a list re-derived inside each fold. A value near zero means the sequential filter did not leak; a clearly positive value would mean the reported feature-selection numbers are optimistic and the honest figure is the nested one.
